method: Deterministic summary of computed figures. No language model is used.
national: One Nation led national search interest in the week to 13 November, averaging 27.1 on Google's 0-100 scale, 4.8 times the next party (Labor). That is 66% of all search interest across the parties tracked.
One Nation fell furthest, down 4.0 points (-13%).

Searches for One Nation jumped to 55 on 3 November, 2.1 times the previous week's average. Coverage around that day: “One Nation volunteer allegedly beaten with bat after dispute over signage” (ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation).
Fastest-rising searches alongside One Nation: “mike newman”, “mike newman one nation”, “one nation hastie cartoon”.
victoria: 13 days until Victorians vote on Saturday 28 November 2026.

Across the latest poll from each of 7 pollsters, the Coalition averages 31.5% of the primary vote, Labor 22.2%, One Nation 20.7% and the Greens 14.4%. On two-party-preferred the Coalition leads 55.6 to 44.4 (5 polls), a 10.6-point swing to the Coalition since 2022.
Applied uniformly to the 2022 pendulum, that swing points to a Coalition majority (60 seats, 45 needed). Treat this as the classic two-party read only: it cannot see One Nation winning seats.
The Roy Morgan MRP (March 2026 - September 2026), which models seats one by one, projects Coalition 62, Labor 40, One Nation 11 and Greens 6: a majority.
Preferred premier (RedBridge/Accent, 3–10 Nov 2026): Wilson 29%, Carroll 18%, Pickering 11%.

One Nation led Victorian search interest in the week to 13 November, averaging 61.9 on Google's 0-100 scale, 5.3 times the next party (the Liberals). That is 68% of all search interest across the parties tracked.
Among the leaders, search interest ran Wilson 69%, Carroll 20%, Pickering 10%, Sandell 1% of the combined total this week.
